transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

It could be the battery, but given your filters are clean and blockages checked, we need to distinguish between a power issue and an airflow protection issue. If the vacuum cuts out after just 5-10 seconds even when fully charged on normal mode (not Boost), it is likely the battery has lost its capacity or the protection circuit is triggering due to age. However, if the charging light never comes on, the charger or contacts might be at fault. Does the charging light come on when you plug it in?
Yes, the charger light comes on and the plug goes in properly. It shows full blue lights when charged. It's mostly worse on Max, and no burning smell or anything like that.

Since it cuts out so quickly even when charged, we need to see if this happens on all settings or just high power. Boost/Max mode drains a five-year-old battery very fast, which can look like a fault but is often normal behaviour under load. Please try running it on the standard (normal) setting for a full room and tell me how long it lasts before cutting out.

On normal it's better, sometimes it does a whole room, but it still cuts out now and then. It's more likely to stop when the battery's partly used rather than straight off the charger. The battery isn't swollen or hot, by the way.

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
At five years old, the cells will have lost capacity and can no longer sustain the voltage required for consistent operation. This is a known wear-out pattern for cordless vacuums of this age. You would need to replace the battery pack; as I cannot confirm the exact part compatibility for 'V ONES', please check Dyson’s official support site or contact their customer service for the correct replacement unit.
